announced on Wednesday that it expanded its partnership with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing
to support AI and HPC chip designs.
The CDNS design and signoff tools are now certified for TSMC’s A14 and N2P processes, while its IP portfolio includes silicon-proven technologies for N3P and N2P.
The companies are expanding support for 3D-IC and advanced packaging, including TSMC’s 3DFabric technology designed to scale systems with hundreds of chiplets.
The company also has silicon-proven IP for TSMC’s N3P and N2P processes for AI and HPC applications.
Global Unichip is already using CDNS solutions for AI accelerators and hyperscale systems on TSMC’s advanced processes.
Overall, the expanded partnership strengthens the company's role in the design software, IP, and packaging tools needed for increasingly complex AI chips.
On the market side, the CDNS stock traded ~2.64% higher at ~$310.76.

title: Cadence expands TSMC partnership for next-gen AI chips
